messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "Just got word from someone close — they’re already packing essentials, quietly. The quiet ones are the ones who’ve made up their minds. Let’s keep our heads down, but stay sharp."
Sender 2: "The signals are too consistent to ignore — it’s not just unrest, it’s a system unraveling. I’ve stopped trying to predict what happens next; the only real question now is how we prepare for what comes after."
Sender 3: "The mood’s changed — people are talking, even in the open. I’ve got a feeling things are shifting, but we’ll watch and wait."
Sender 4: "The kids’ school pickup line feels different lately — quieter, like people are holding their breath. I’d say things are shifting, but not sure yet if it’s a storm building or just a bad season. Be careful what you say, even in passing."
Sender 5: "The leaves are falling early this year — not just on the trees, but in the offices and on the faces of people who used to know their place. I’ve started noticing the same quiet in different neighborhoods, and the jokes have that new kind of weight. Whatever’s coming, it feels like the ground is shifting under us, but slowly. Keep your ears open."
Sender 6: "The power grid’s been acting up again—just like last month, but this time the lights stayed out longer. Seems like even the backups are getting tired. Let’s keep our heads down, but also keep our ears open."
Sender 7: "The border checks are running smooth again, and I heard the old bakery on 5th finally got its flour delivery — but the silence from the official news is louder than any broadcast. Let’s keep our heads down, but stay sharp."
Sender 8: "The kids’ school’s still open, but the teachers haven’t been paid in weeks — and the quiet talk among parents lately feels different, like people are bracing for something. Be careful what you say, even in small talk."
Sender 9: "The tea house chatter’s changed — people aren’t just complaining anymore. Something’s shifting, and the silence from the usual sources is louder than any announcement. Be careful."
Sender 10: "Just got word from someone in the old district — the shop on the corner finally reopened, but the owner’s packing up his other locations. Said the city’s humming too quiet, like before a storm. We should keep our heads down, but stay sharp."

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 10 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 10.
